title.value: Personalized Prediction of Future Lesion Activity and Treatment Effect in Multiple Sclerosis from Baseline MRI
title.justification: The extracted paper's title explicitly refers to personalized prediction in MS, which aligns with precision medicine.
title.quote: Personalized Prediction of Future Lesion Activity and Treatment Effect in Multiple Sclerosis from Baseline MRI

extractions.description: The paper presents a deep neural network model for personalized treatment decisions in multiple sclerosis, using baseline MRI and available clinical data. It predicts future lesion activity and estimates treatment effects for various treatment options, validated on a large dataset of MRI scans from clinical trials.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on precision medicine and treatment optimization for multiple sclerosis, which, while important for healthcare development, does not directly relate to climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Precision medicine for chronic diseases such as multiple sclerosis involves choosing a treatment which best balances efficacy and side effects/preferences for individual patients.

primary_sub_category.quote: Our model (a) predicts future new and enlarging T2 weighted (NE-T2) lesion counts on follow-up MRI on multiple treatments and (b) estimates the conditional average treatment effect (CATE).

applications.quote: To this end, we present the first deep neural network model for individualized treatment decisions from baseline magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for MS patients.
